reserveReview.reviewer: NR-EURQ review 2026-10-21 of the Quantoz snapshot dated 2026-10-14
reserveReview.rationale: Re-reviewed 2026-10-21 against Quantoz's transparency page, which now publishes a snapshot dated 14 October 2026 (time datetime 2026-10-14) reporting EURQ tokens in circulation of EUR 4,289,619, a 100.47% reserve ratio and a whole-number composition of 35% cash and 65% government bonds. The two published categories now total 100%, so the previous snapshot's unexplained percentage point is closed by the issuer's own figures rather than renormalised or inferred. The 30 August 2026 snapshot (33% cash, 66% bonds, 100.76%) is superseded as the current composition and is not carried forward. The reserve policy still identifies euro government bonds as Dutch and German; bank identities, bond security identifiers, country weights, maturities and independent assurance remain undisclosed.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Quantoz transparency published reserve snapshot dated 14 October 2026 (EURQ cash 35%, government bonds 65%); no separate underlying balance date is disclosed
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The published percentages are complete at 100%, but Quantoz does not identify individual banking partners, bond security identifiers, country weights or a maximum maturity, and the government-bond liquidity horizon remains unknown. The 100.47% reserve ratio and the token circulation figure are issuer self-reporting, not independent assurance or a complete reserve-to-liability reconciliation.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: The whitepaper identifies Stichting Quantoz as the bankruptcy-remote safeguarding entity and separate reserve accounts. The current transparency page describes multiple Tier 1 European banks but does not name the banks, securities custodians, provider allocations, or asset-reuse terms. Protection against issuer insolvency does not eliminate bank or investment risk.
